subject: OrionHealth request: Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) & cross-border evidence
messages:

Subject: OrionHealth: Transfer Impact Assessment request for Redwood inference

Hi Karthik,

We are starting our DPIA / cross-border review for the integration proof-of-concept and need to complete a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) for Redwood. Specifically, our privacy team is looking for:

- A completed TIA matrix (we have a template attached if that helps)
- Where processing occurs (EU region, US region, or both) and whether subprocessors transfer data outside the EEA
- The contractual mechanism you use for cross-border transfers (SCCs, BCRs, adequacy, other) and a signed copy if available
- Details on technical controls: at-rest and in-transit encryption, key management (KMS/HSM), pseudonymization options, and logs retained for uploads/ingestion
- Whether Redwood can run in a private VPC in an EU region for customer-dedicated deployments (we may require on-prem or EU-only hosting)

Can you confirm the timeline for providing the TIA and any evidentiary artifacts (sample logs, SCC copy, brief architecture diagram)? We are aiming to complete our internal review by 2026-05-20.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Schmidt
Privacy Lead — OrionHealth
privacy.ops@orionhealth.com

Subject: Re: OrionHealth: Transfer Impact Assessment request for Redwood inference

Hi Lena — thanks for the request and for sending your template. We've completed a first-pass TIA and attached the completed spreadsheet. Summary highlights: 

- Transfer mechanisms: Redwood executes EU & UK SCCs (standard contractual clauses) for controller-processor relationships. A signed copy of our SCC annex is attached (SCC_Redwood_signed_v1.pdf) and we can execute customer-specific exhibits as required.
- Processing locations: Our hosted API runs in region-specific clusters; customer data for OrionHealth's production workload can be restricted to EU regions when on Dedicated or Private deployments. For our multi-tenant hosted offering, some processing may occur on servers located in the US — we provide SCCs for those transfers.
- Subprocessors: We publish a subprocessors list in our security documentation. We confirm that some managed services (monitoring/metrics) are operated by third-party vendors that may be US-based; these are covered by SCCs.
- Encryption and keys: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. Customers using Redwood Private/Dedicated can bring their own KMS or use our KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). HSM-backed keys are available for enterprise contracts.
- Pseudonymization & minimization: We support tokenization/pseudonymization patterns and can provide guidance for minimizing identifiers in logs.
- Logs & retention: Sample upload logs are included (redwood_upload_log_sample.csv). We retain audit logs per customer-configured retention; standard retention is 90 days for request logs and 365 days for billing trace logs, configurable for Dedicated/Private contracts.
- DPIA support: We can provide a short architectural diagram and a partner statement to support your DPIA; if you need a formal DPIA opinion, we can coordinate with our legal team.

Clarifying question: can you confirm the categories of personal data OrionHealth expects to send (PII, health attributes, pseudonymized IDs)? That will help us tailor the DPIA statement and retention recommendations.

Drive link to artifacts: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C4d5E6f_TIA-evidence

Attachments: TIA_OrionHealth_filled.xlsx; redwood_upload_log_sample.csv; SCC_Redwood_signed_v1.pdf

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy — Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Naomi — this is great, thank you. We attached our filled TIA (TIA_OrionHealth_filled.xlsx) with a couple of follow-up items: 

- Can you confirm whether the sample upload log includes IP addresses and which fields are redacted in the standard retention export? We need a record-level example to satisfy our IT security review.
- On SCCs: can you confirm whether Redwood has an executed SCC that covers subprocessors, or if customers must execute separate subprocessor addenda?
- We may require that processing for test and UAT environments stay within the EU. Is that available for POC?

If possible, could you provide the architecture diagram and the sample logs by EOD 2026-05-14? That will keep us on track for our internal review.

Thanks,
Lena

Hi Lena — attaching the items requested and answering the quick technical questions below.

Quick answers:
- Sample log contents: our upload log sample (redwood_upload_log_sample.csv) includes timestamps, request IDs, object size, user agent; by default standard exports redact full IP addresses (last octet masked) but can be configured to remove IPs entirely per customer policy.
- SCC coverage: Redwood's executed SCC_Redwood_signed_v1 covers processor-subprocessor transfers for our standard terms; if OrionHealth requires a separate subprocessor addendum, we can execute a customer-specific exhibit.
- EU-only POC processing: available on Dedicated or Private trial — we can provision an EU-only test stack for the POC. For hosted multi-tenant POC, data may transit non-EU regions.

Attached: redwood_upload_log_sample.csv; SCC_Redwood_signed_v1.pdf
